unit.title: Models with numbers: variables, constraints, objective

lesson.title: From words to a model
lesson.subtitle: Variables, constraints and an objective, for the school lunch

video.title: From words to a model
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor Eze — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor in the school kitchen with the cook; a plate, a price list and a small coin purse.
scenes.animation: Food icons pop onto the plate; the purse shrinks.
scenes.narration: The school kitchen has a new rule: every lunch must give pupils enough energy, protein and iron. And the money is tight. The cook asked me: what’s the cheapest plate that’s still enough?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: from words to a model, so a hard choice becomes numbers we can check.

scenes.visual: Six food cards, each with an empty box beside it: rice, beans, egg, milk, greens, groundnuts.
scenes.animation: A question mark appears in each box, then turns into a letter.
scenes.narration: A model starts with the decisions, written as variables. Here: how many portions of each food. Call them rice, beans, greens and so on: each one a number, with a unit, cups or handfuls.

scenes.visual: The energy sum builds term by term on a card, then the ≥ 700 appears; protein and iron lines follow.
scenes.animation: Each term types in as it is said.
scenes.narration: Next, each limit becomes an inequality. A cup of rice gives two hundred and sixty kilocalories, a handful of groundnuts one hundred and seventy, and so on. Add them up: the total must be at least seven hundred. Protein must be at least twenty grams, and iron at least five milligrams.

scenes.visual: A price tag on each food; the cost expression builds; an arrow points down: minimise.
scenes.animation: Prices drop onto the expression; the arrow pulses down.
scenes.narration: Then the goal, written as one expression: the cost. Fifteen coins a cup of rice, eight a handful of groundnuts, and so on. Make it as small as possible.

scenes.visual: Three stacked cards, variables, constraints, objective, snap together into one box labelled model.
scenes.animation: Cards slide together; the box closes.
scenes.narration: Variables, constraints and an objective: together, that’s a model. Constraint is the maths word for a limit, and objective for the goal. A good model says what matters, and nothing that isn’t true.

scenes.visual: The usual plate; three gauges fill: energy and protein pass, iron stops far short in red.
scenes.animation: Gauges fill one by one; the iron gauge flashes.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check a plan: put the numbers in
scenes.narration: Now any plan can be checked. The usual plate: two cups of rice, an egg and a cup of milk. Energy: seven hundred and forty-five, fine. Protein: twenty-four, fine. Iron: only one point eight milligrams. So it isn’t feasible, at sixty coins.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor holds the plate; the sum 230 + 340 on a card. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A plate has one cup of beans and two handfuls of groundnuts. Energy: two hundred and thirty, plus three hundred and forty. Does it meet the energy limit?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets a check. Then the cheapest plate appears with its price tag, 41.
scenes.animation: Check pops; the new plate slides in.
scenes.narration: No: five hundred and seventy is less than seven hundred, so the plate isn’t feasible. Putting the numbers in is all it takes to check. Finding the cheapest feasible plate is harder: the simplex method finds it, at forty-one coins.

scenes.visual: A plate piled with groundnuts; a pupil shakes her head; a new rule card is written: variety, allergies.
scenes.animation: The pile grows; a warning tag swings in; the rule card slides into the model box.
scenes.on_screen_text: The model knows only your rules
scenes.narration: But would pupils eat it? The model knows nothing about taste, variety or allergies. Allow four handfuls, and the cheapest plate is nearly all groundnuts. If a rule matters, write it into the model, with the cook and the pupils.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: food buttons, three need bars, a cost counter and a Find the cheapest button.
scenes.animation: A finger taps foods; bars fill; the cheapest plate appears.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: School lunch for less
scenes.narration: In the app, build a plate yourself and watch each need fill up. Serve the usual plate, then ask for the cheapest. Which needs are met exactly, and which come free?

scenes.visual: Ms Salma holds a model card with the objective line missing. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A colleague’s lunch model has the variables and every limit, but no goal. What will a solver give him?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets the check; four summary lines and a takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Any plate that fits, maybe a costly one: without a goal, there’s no “best”. Remember: decisions become variables, limits become inequalities, and the goal becomes one expression. Check a plan by putting its numbers in. And a model knows only the rules you write.

scenes.visual: Salma’s class: the board with three headings; groups hold up their plans; ticks and crosses beside them.
scenes.animation: Plans appear; ticks and crosses pop.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: model a class purchase with your pupils. Exercise books and pens, a budget, and how many of each the class needs. Write the variables, limits and goal on the board. Then check each group’s plan with the numbers.

checkpoints.prompt: One cup of beans and two handfuls of groundnuts: 230 + 340 kcal. Does it meet the energy limit of 700?

options.text: We can’t tell without the prices

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 230 + 340 = 570, less than 700, so this plate isn’t feasible.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — 230 + 340 = 570, and the limit says at least 700. Prices don’t matter for a limit on energy.

checkpoints.prompt: A model has variables and every limit, but no goal. What will a solver give?

options.text: Any plate that keeps the limits, maybe a costly one

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — with no objective, any feasible plan answers the question. “Best” needs a goal.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the solver will find a plan that keeps every limit, but with no goal it has no reason to pick a cheap one.
